source_snapshot.procedure: Configure explicitly inaccurate threshold/window placeholders, inject several correctable memory errors below threshold, wait and inspect decay.
source_snapshot.criteria: Count falls after the time window while health remains normal, slot records are correct and lights remain off.
source_snapshot.deepseek: PARTIAL; generic CE logs do not prove bucket arithmetic.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: Requires authoritative bucket values, targets, counter timeline and recovery.

old_problem: The defining threshold, units, window, decay rule, counter source, safe injection cardinality and controller target matrix were absent; the source even labels its values inaccurate.
disposition_reason: The intended numerical experiment is unambiguous: remain below an approved CE threshold and demonstrate time-based decay. ED-03 allows platform threshold/window/counter/target values to be bound as project configuration, while ED-15 forbids a PASS until they are supplied and ED-16 gates injection. The review therefore rejects the inaccurate placeholders and defines auditable arithmetic without inventing numbers.
decision_basis: Read Reliability row 29, its AI fields, record 2433 and next pending row 30.
Kept every controller target and the below-threshold decay identity.
Converted vague `several times` into an owner-calculated count with explicit margin.
Made samples from one authoritative counter and monotonic timestamps decisive.
No BIOS or fault-injection operation was attempted.

test_case.purpose: For each approved memory-controller tuple, prove a bounded CE series increments the designated bucket below threshold and that the counter decays according to the signed platform time rule.
required_package: Authoritative threshold, units, time window, decay algorithm and counter source
Supported injector build/hash and CE semantics
Calculated below-threshold count/margin and expected event/health oracle
Abort, recovery and BIOS restoration plan
test_case.test_command: Reject all `(Inaccurate)` values. For one mapped controller at a time, capture the counter baseline, have the FAE inject the approved CE count, timestamp every sample, verify distance from threshold, wait the exact configured window, measure the specified decay, correlate slot/indicator/health evidence, then restore settings.
test_case.expected_result: Every mapped controller shows the approved increment and post-window reduction from the same counter without reaching escalation threshold; system health is normal, correct slot evidence is present, lights stay off and state is restored.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires signed bucket parameters, complete target coverage, monotonic counter series matching the approved arithmetic, demonstrated threshold margin, expected slot logs, no-light/health proof and restoration. Generic CE text or guessed timing/threshold cannot pass.
safety_gate: Dedicated idle SUT and independent console.
Calculate count and margin from the approved threshold before injecting one target.
Abort on unexpected counter movement, threshold approach, UCE, lamp, hang or health change.
No automatic retry; preserve evidence before recovery.
expected_evidence: Bucket specification and signed target matrix
Package hash and bounded count calculation
Windows/BMC/applicable UEFI slot and indicator evidence
test_case.recovery: Stop before escalation on any mismatch, preserve the counter/event timeline, and let the authorized operator restore bucket/EDKII settings and verify memory health before separate approval of another run.

source_conflict.reason: Inaccurate source values are explicitly invalidated and replaced only by signed runtime bindings plus measurable counter arithmetic.

blocked.reason: The test semantics and safe acceptance method are complete; project-specific numeric values are execution prerequisites.
